solves.reasoning: (A) evaluating — a reference group is used as a frame for evaluating one's behavior; ignoring contradicts the purpose. (B) contribution — members feel proud about their contribution to community service; indifference contradicts pride. (C) imitating — the normative effect involves imitating the reference group; rejecting contradicts normative following.

(A) standards — members evaluate themselves by the group's standards; failures contradicts self-evaluation by standards. (B) comparison — reference groups have comparison effects; identical effects makes no grammatical/conceptual sense. (C) negative — comparing yourself to shining classmates leads to negative self-evaluation; positive contradicts the resulting feeling that performance 'is not up to par'.

(A) normative — 'the normative effect' is the passage's key term; destructive contradicts the positive self-evaluation described. (B) associative — passage explicitly says 'associative effects'; divisive contradicts the passage's 'associative'. (C) par — 'not up to par' is an idiom meaning below standard; average changes the idiom and is awkward.

③ 'favorable' is wrong: 'you may have a favorable self-evaluation, feeling that your academic performance is not up to par' — favorable (좋은/유리한) contradicts 'not up to par' which describes a negative outcome. The passage says 'negative self-evaluation'.

④ 'struggle' is wrong: 'if most of your classmates struggle in academic achievement' — the comparison effect requires classmates who excel, not struggle. The passage says 'shine in academic achievement'. Struggling classmates wouldn't cause negative self-comparison.
④ 'divisive' is wrong: passage says 'associative effects' — associative means connecting/linking. Divisive (분열시키는) is the opposite. The brilliant group association makes you feel proud, not divided.

Blank: 'feel proud about their ___ to a community service project'. Members of a volunteer organization feel proud about what they gave/provided = contribution (기여). Opposition/resistance/withdrawal all contradict volunteering.

Blank: 'the normative effect basically involves ___ the reference group'. Normative effect = following norms = imitating (모방하기). Avoiding/challenging/dismissing all contradict the normative following behavior.

Blank: 'basking in ___ glory'. The phrase 'basking in reflected glory' is an idiom meaning enjoying the glory of a group you belong to. 'Reflected' (반사된) is the correct word — the glory reflects onto you from the group.
evaluating = assessing (평가하다). Eliminating (제거), establishing (확립), overlooking (간과) are wrong. Evaluating/assessing both mean judging the value/quality of something.
normative = prescriptive (규범적인). Destructive (파괴적인), optional (선택적인), accidental (우연한) are all wrong. Normative = relating to a norm/standard = prescriptive (규범을 규정하는).
shine (빛나다/뛰어나다) = excel (탁월하다). Fail (실패), participate (참여), withdraw (철수) are wrong. To 'shine in academic achievement' = to excel in academics.
proud (자랑스러운)의 반의어 = ashamed (부끄러운). Confident/satisfied/hopeful are all positive feelings similar to proud. Ashamed is the direct antonym.
brilliant (뛰어난/훌륭한)의 반의어 = mediocre (평범한/보통의). Talented/remarkable/distinguished are all synonyms of brilliant. Mediocre means of only average quality — the direct antonym.

(A) 'This positive self-evaluation reflects the normative effect' — reflects = 반영하다 (to show/represent). (B) 'The mirror reflects the light' — reflects = 반사하다 (to bounce back light). So (A)반영하다 - (B)반사하다 = choice 2.

'A group that a person uses as a standard for measuring/evaluating their own attitudes, values, and behavior' = reference group (준거집단). Peer group/support group/focus group don't match this definition.
contribute (동사) → contribution (명사). 'Feel proud about their contribution to a community service project' — noun form needed after possessive 'their'.
norm (명사) → normative (형용사). 'The normative effect of a reference group' — adjective form modifying 'effect'.

Blank: 'reference groups can also have comparison effects and associative effects on ___'. These effects impact how people judge themselves = self-appraisals (자기평가). Group membership/academic records/community projects don't match.

Blank: 'you, too, are likely to ___'. The normative effect means you follow the group's norms. If parents have high self-esteem, you adopt the same = 'share that norm and have high self-esteem'. Choice 2 matches the passage exactly.
